entries.title: Spoken Summary
entries.description: The founding flow: a voice memo in, a spoken TL;DR out, transcript saved on the side.

entries.title: Meeting Minutes
entries.description: One transcript, three concurrent readings — decisions, action items, risks — assembled into one minutes document.

entries.title: Podcast Show Notes
entries.description: Episode audio to publishable show notes: summary, chapter list from the transcript's time marks, pull quotes, and a title.

entries.title: Interview to Article
entries.description: Interview audio becomes a quote-faithful article, pushed through one refine loop before it ships.

entries.title: Weekly Voice Journal
entries.description: A folder of the week's memos, each transcribed and boiled down, joined under a theme title.

entries.title: Contract Clause Scan
entries.description: Every section of a contract mined into a clause table, topped with a plain-words risk brief. (A reading aid, not legal advice.)

entries.title: Paper Digest
entries.description: A research paper read at two depths at once — abstract-level and "what could we apply" — merged into one digest.

entries.title: Policy Diff Brief
entries.description: Two versions of a document, the mechanical diff, and a human-readable "what changed for you."

entries.title: Invoice Ledger
entries.description: A folder of invoice PDFs becomes a ledger table, a spend chart, and a markdown report.

entries.title: Book Summary
entries.description: The map-reduce classic: a cheap model summarizes every chunk, a strong model writes the one page that ships. `{index}` labels each paragraph with its section number on the way in — free, since the `<each>` already knows the position; the reduce step reads a numbered outline instead of 148 anonymous paragraphs.

entries.title: Reflexion Writer
entries.description: The draft–critique–revise loop, budgeted. The critic can't rewrite; the reviser can't re-judge; the Gate decides when it's done arguing.

entries.title: Channel Blast
entries.description: One set of launch notes, three channel-native versions written concurrently, each saved to its own file.

entries.title: Translate Three
entries.description: The same document localized into three languages concurrently.

entries.title: Frontmatter Bot
entries.description: A finished blog post gains its metadata: SEO title, meta description, tags — generated concurrently, assembled as frontmatter.

entries.title: House Style
entries.description: Rewrite a draft to match your style guide — with a diff so you can see exactly what the model touched.

entries.title: Ingest a Folder
entries.description: The index-time half of every RAG flow: a folder of PDFs becomes a searchable index. Run once; re-run when documents change.

entries.title: Ask Your Docs
entries.description: The query-time half: one question, five retrieved passages, one grounded answer — every step inspectable.

entries.title: Chat With Your Docs
entries.description: The parked-run chat session: follow-up questions resolved against the conversation journal, the whole session saved as a file.

entries.title: Corrective RAG
entries.description: Retrieval that checks its own evidence and retries with a better question — three tries, then best-effort, visibly.

entries.title: Two-Index Analyst
entries.description: An agent that chooses which index to search, when to compute, and when to finish — within a budget, transcript readable.

entries.title: Photos for the Web
entries.description: A folder of photos resized and watermarked, one corrupt file no longer killing the batch.

entries.title: Screenshots to How-To
entries.description: A folder of numbered screenshots becomes a written guide: OCR reads the UI text, a vision model describes the action, a writer stitches the steps.

entries.title: Alt-Text Writer
entries.description: Accessibility at batch scale: one factual alt-text line per image.

entries.title: Video Clip Notes
entries.description: A webinar recording mined for its cuttable moments, plus a thumbnail.

entries.title: Photo Cull List
entries.description: A vision model flags the blurry and blinked; you get a keep/reject list to act on in your photo app. (The flow writes a list — moving your photos stays your hand's job, per the effects rule.)

entries.title: CSV Insights
entries.description: A sales CSV becomes a chart and three written insights — the table the model saw sitting right beside its claims.

entries.title: Survey Themes
entries.description: Free-text survey responses tagged by sentiment; the negatives distilled into the five themes leadership will actually read.

entries.title: Ticket Trends
entries.description: A folder of support tickets structured into (product, issue, severity) and charted — the weekly meeting's opening slide.

entries.title: Log Triage
entries.description: Mostly instant rows: errors filtered and deduped in code, one model call to hypothesize root causes.

entries.title: Receipts to Expenses
entries.description: Phone photos of receipts become a categorized expense report with a spend chart.

entries.title: Research Brief

entries.title: Minutes Name Fix

entries.title: ReAct Agent
entries.description: The canonical agent: a Think that picks tools, tool chains that `resume`, a budget that proves it ends. A named block — no framework.

entries.title: Plan and Execute
entries.description: A planner decomposes the task; an `<each>` runs one agent per sub-question; a Gate decides whether the merged report needs another pass.

entries.title: Tiny-First Batch
entries.description: The cascade economics flow: the fast model transcribes everything; only the garbled pay for the big one. The `×N` on row 2.4 is the invoice.

entries.title: Frontier Escalation
entries.description: Local RAG answers; a Gate checks grounding; only demonstrably weak answers send their (locally retrieved) context to a frontier model.

entries.title: Router Desk
entries.description: A classifier routes each ticket to its specialist; the branches converge on one reviewed draft. (The two specialist blocks are entries 41-style agents over their own indexes.)

entries.title: Index Self-Test
entries.description: The index examines itself: generate questions from the corpus, answer each, check retrieval and grounding separately.

entries.title: Golden Regression
entries.description: The suite-as-a-diff: run your flow over its cases, compare against the accepted baseline, read only what moved. Shown pre-filled with a trivial one-row placeholder (SPEC-Q124) so a fresh install runs end to end immediately — replace `flow_under_test`'s child row with your own flow to actually use this for regression testing.

entries.title: A/B Judge
entries.description: Two systems, one judge, win counts — which prompt (or model, or pipeline) actually wins on your cases. `system_a`/`system_b` are shown pre-filled with the same trivial placeholder (SPEC-Q124) purely so this installs and runs immediately — replace each with your real two systems to actually compare them.

entries.title: Model Migration
entries.description: "Can we switch to the cheaper model?" — the suite run twice by parameter, the differences reviewed by a human, `keep` by default.
entries.notRunnableReason: Row 1 uses 'RunSuite', which isn't a task this version of Flows knows.

entries.title: Nightly Drift
entries.description: The suite that remembers: every night's report appends to a journal, so the analysis can say "those failures are back."

entries.title: Self-Ingesting Inbox
entries.description: Drop a PDF into the folder and it's searchable minutes later. The trigger is the doorbell; the flow re-ingests the folder; per-item caching means each run only pays for the file that just arrived.

entries.title: Auto-Transcribe Drop
entries.description: Entry 43's cascade, armed: record a memo, and by the time you're at your desk the notes file is beside it — the big model paid only for garbled audio.

entries.title: Morning Briefing

entries.title: Receipts Ledger, Always On
entries.description: Two small armed flows cooperating through a context file — photograph receipts whenever, get the spend report every Sunday — with the capture flow watching its own pile too: `Count Context` and `Compare`, both instant, flag a busy week before Sunday with no model call.

entries.title: Order Triage Queue
entries.description: A local SQLite store that remembers order status across runs — no round trip through files between them. New orders land, anything over threshold gets flagged for a human, everything else auto-approves, and a model is only spent on the orders that actually need judgement.

entries.title: The Parser You Already Wrote
entries.description: A folder of vendor invoices in your own shop's plain-text export format — not OCR, not a model guessing at a `total:` line, just the three-line parser your billing team has trusted for years, called from a row instead of a cron job. Compare with entry 9 (Invoice Ledger), which reaches for a model because its invoices are scanned images with no fixed format to parse against.

entries.title: A Nightly Ledger From Your Own Script
entries.description: Both doors, armed: a usage export lands overnight in a format only your own parser understands; the code door turns one file into rows, the store door remembers them across every night this has ever run, and the morning total is one query away — not a re-read of every file that ever landed.

entries.title: Normalize the Exports
entries.description: A folder of CSV exports whose headers never quite agree — an agent free-forms inside a fenced `workdir` until they're one table. This is the improvise-then-promote arc: run it once with `Improvise`, then let `catflow promote` turn whatever it did that maps to a plain read into an ordinary row, keeping only the genuinely ad hoc part improvised.

entries.description: `Generate Sound` (MusicGen) is `Speak`'s sibling — same signature, different job: music instead of a voice reading text.

entries.title: Eight Seeds, One Sheet
entries.description: The pattern the whole column exists for: a `Range` drives an `<each>` generate, and a real `Contact Sheet` tiles the results labelled by what changed — eight images, read as one.

entries.title: Drive the Latent Yourself
entries.description: The latent I/O column, as a `.catpipeline`: `Init Latent` creates the noise, `Denoise` runs a named number of steps over it, `Decode Latent` turns it back into pixels — the intermediate that makes "more steps under your own control" a row instead of a feature request.
entries.notRunnableReason: a .catpipeline (model-space flow), which this version doesn't support

entries.title: Blend Two Checkpoints
entries.description: Model space, and the other CLI verb: a `gives: model` pipeline can't `catflow run` — it produces no asset and never appears as a row. `catflow models materialize` is what actually builds it: `Load Checkpoint` and `Blend` merge two pinned checkpoints' real weights (`method=linear`), the recipe hash is the blend's identity, and materializing writes a derived manifest under the pipeline's own name — no `Pin Model` needed, since naming *is* what materializing does (that row is for pinning a model *mid*-pipeline, where the pipeline's own output is something else and nothing would otherwise name it). `--preview` renders a fixed-prompt probe image of the merge itself, not a stand-in. Verified for real, both ways: `Base Style` and `Alt Style` name the same checkpoint here (no second, genuinely different Z-Image-family checkpoint published yet), so this is `merge(A, A, ratio) == A` — a real merge, real weights, correct by an invariant that doesn't need a second checkpoint to check, and the materialized result actually generates. Point `Alt Style` at a real second Z-Image-family checkpoint the day one exists, and this same pipeline blends them for real.
entries.notRunnableReason: a .catpipeline (model-space flow), which this version doesn't support

entries.title: Pick a Look
entries.description: Presets (Q199): a `.catpipeline` bundles named settings behind one caller-facing knob, so `steps=`/`width=`/`height=` never has to leak into a business user's own file. `presets:` declares three looks; `preset=(param:quality)` binds whichever one the caller names through `params:` — the row itself never says `steps=9`, only "the look I was given." A `.cat` caller picks one the same way it picks any other value: `uses: PickALook.catpipeline as Look` then `2. Look  (1); quality=studio` — no `preset=` in sight, because presets are pipeline-only.
entries.notRunnableReason: a .catpipeline (model-space flow), which this version doesn't support
